name: The last week of the year
meaning: The long green season after Pentecost, ending with Christ the King on the last Sunday before Advent.
summary: The long green season after Pentecost, ending with Christ the King on the last Sunday before Advent.

name: Advent
meaning: Four weeks of waiting and watching before Christmas. The readings look forward to the coming of Christ, at Bethlehem and at the end of all things, and the church gets quieter rather than louder.
practices: One more candle on the wreath each Sunday|Advent Lessons and Carols on the first Sunday evening|A Wednesday study on the Gospel of Mark|Blue Christmas, a quiet service for anyone finding December hard
summary: Four weeks of waiting and watching before Christmas. The readings look forward to the coming of Christ, at Bethlehem and at the end of all things, and the church gets quieter rather than louder.

name: Christmas
meaning: Twelve days, not one. The feast starts on Christmas Eve and runs to the eve of the Epiphany, and the white and gold stay up the whole time.
practices: Christmas Eve at 4:00 and 10:30|Christmas Day said Eucharist|Watchnight prayers on New Year's Eve|Carols every Sunday until the Epiphany
summary: Twelve days, not one. The feast starts on Christmas Eve and runs to the eve of the Epiphany, and the white and gold stay up the whole time.

name: Epiphany
meaning: The Magi arrive, Jesus is baptized, and the Sundays that follow are about light reaching further: the first disciples, the first signs, the first sermons.
practices: Chalk blessing for front doors on the Epiphany|Twelfth Night supper|Candlemas on February 2
summary: The Magi arrive, Jesus is baptized, and the Sundays that follow are about light reaching further: the first disciples, the first signs, the first sermons.

name: Lent
meaning: Forty days from Ash Wednesday, a season for simplifying, giving and starting again. The flowers come out, the alleluias stop, and the Tuesday soup suppers start.
practices: Ash Wednesday at 7:00 and 19:00|Soup suppers and a study every Tuesday|Stations of the Cross on Fridays|The pantry's Lent food drive
summary: Forty days from Ash Wednesday, a season for simplifying, giving and starting again. The flowers come out, the alleluias stop, and the Tuesday soup suppers start.

name: Holy Week
meaning: From the palms of Palm Sunday through the Last Supper, the cross and the long wait of Holy Saturday.
practices: Palm procession around the green|Maundy Thursday foot washing and the stripping of the altar|Good Friday at noon|The Easter Vigil on Saturday night
summary: From the palms of Palm Sunday through the Last Supper, the cross and the long wait of Holy Saturday.

name: Easter
meaning: Fifty days of Easter, longer than Lent. White and gold, lilies, and the alleluias back, loudly.
practices: Easter Day at 8:00 and 10:30 with brass|Baptisms at the Vigil|The Easter egg hunt on the green
summary: Fifty days of Easter, longer than Lent. White and gold, lilies, and the alleluias back, loudly.

name: Pentecost
meaning: The Spirit comes in wind and fire. Wear red; the readings are read in several languages at once.
practices: Readings in five languages|Confirmations with the bishop|A parish picnic after the 10:30
summary: The Spirit comes in wind and fire. Wear red; the readings are read in several languages at once.

name: Season after Pentecost
meaning: The long green season of growth: the Sundays work through a Gospel chapter by chapter, and the parish works through its garden, its summer camp and its autumn harvest.
practices: Summer evening Eucharist in the garden|Vacation Bible school in July|Harvest supper in October|All Saints and the reading of names
summary: The long green season of growth: the Sundays work through a Gospel chapter by chapter, and the parish works through its garden, its summer camp and its autumn harvest.
